title: CI/CD Pipeline Setup Guide: Practical Evaluation and Implementation
description: A practical Developer Tools guide to ci/cd pipeline setup, covering requirements, evidence-based evaluation, a realistic pilot, rollout, cost, and risk controls.
author: PilotStack Editorial Team

sections.title: Problem and Scope
sections.body: A CI/CD pipeline should make changes safer and repeatable, not simply run more jobs. Define the release path from commit to production, the tests that block a release, and the recovery action if deployment fails. Write down the intended outcome, the people affected, the current baseline, and what would count as failure. Separate the problem to solve from preferences for a particular vendor or methodology.

sections.title: Requirements and Evidence
sections.body: For ci/cd pipeline setup, check reproducible dependency installation; test coverage and test data isolation; secret handling; artifact provenance; environment separation; approval gates; deployment health checks; rollback or roll-forward strategy; cache invalidation; and auditability. Separate mandatory requirements from preferences. Record the evidence source and date for every important claim, and label it as confirmed in documentation, verified in a trial, unclear, or unavailable. For developer workflows, validate repository and CI integration, access controls, test coverage, API limits, observability, and rollback procedures.

sections.title: Evaluation Method
sections.body: Use the same scenario and scorecard for each candidate. Weight requirements before comparing products, score each item against evidence, and record trade-offs instead of hiding them in one overall rating. Include usability, administration effort, reliability, accessibility where relevant, support coverage, export options, and the cost of required add-ons.

sections.title: Practical Pilot
sections.body: Start with one low-risk service. Confirm that a clean checkout can build, tests fail when an intentional defect is introduced, secrets are unavailable to untrusted pull requests, and deployment verification checks the live artifact. Simulate a failed health check and verify rollback instructions. Agree on pass/fail criteria before the pilot begins. Compare results with the baseline and record limitations; do not infer performance at scale from a demo or a small sample.

sections.title: Rollout and Ownership
sections.body: Name a business owner and an operational owner. Document setup, migration or configuration, permissions, training, support escalation, and a rollback path. Start with a limited scope, resolve blockers, and expand only when the agreed acceptance criteria are met.

sections.title: Cost, Risk, and Exit
sections.body: Estimate the full cost over the expected use period, including subscription or usage fees, minimum seats, add-ons, implementation, migration, training, administration, and maintenance. Do not treat a green build as proof that production behavior is correct. Avoid sharing production credentials with forked pull requests, and ensure caching cannot reuse stale or untrusted build outputs. Confirm contract terms, service limits, export and deletion procedures, and the steps needed to move away from the solution.

sections.title: Decision Checklist
sections.body: Choose the option that meets the mandatory requirements with acceptable operational risk, not simply the one with the longest feature list. Make the pipeline deterministic, least-privilege, observable, and able to stop or recover a bad release. Record the selected option, alternatives rejected, unresolved risks, cost assumptions, owner, and review date.
